doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: State of jazz today
summary: Styles are separated now; he favors swinging mainstream jazz over angry avant-garde.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Wow. What do you think of the state of jazz these days?

Well it’s strange because there’s such separation between the styles. When I grew up in New York there was one style of playing, but the styles were kind of bebop and swing were combining in a way and there was such mixture of players and musicians that you would be able to function well enough with the next player even though he might have been a different style. It was still close enough, and as long as it swung. That was the important thing, if it swung, to me anyway. And it don’t mean a thing— And today there’s so many different styles of jazz, there’s no real — I hear some of the fusion players and some of the avante garde players putting this music down that we’re playing here, which comes from say the Swing Era, mainstream jazz. And as if to say there’s nothing new being created with mainstream jazz. We’ve got to do something more creative. It’s got to be original. It’s got to be different. Always strive for different. Well we strive for different things, different phrasing, different solos, I try never to play the same solo on a particular song. And so I hear all these other players do that. And there are some great players at this festival and at the festivals that we usually wind up with. I challenge anybody to be as good as some of these players down here. I don’t care what style it is. To me jazz should be a happy, peaceful thing. It should not be an angry jazz form. And I hear a lot of anger coming out in some of this other music. I can try to appreciate it and I do appreciate some of it. I try to find some qualities and some good things in it, but I always have to come back to this style to really find satisfaction say. This is where it’s at really. This is my kind of music. I love it, I enjoy it, and I’m constantly trying to be creative.
